about: Live, opt-in cases for scripts/brain-router-check.ts: who answers a message when the tab is online and has its trained 1B. `labelled`: demo-style simple file and code tasks (the tab) against training, GPU, internet and big-model asks (the cloud); every one must go where its label says. `borderline`: tasks that look simple but need the network, or that ask more than a small model can give, with the brain they should get; reported, not gated.

labelled.message: Let's write some basic code.
Create hello.py that prints hello world and run it.
Make a file ideas.txt listing butter, cheese and tea, one per line.
Rename the variable x to count in counter.js.
How many lines are in notes.txt?
Fix the typo 'recieve' in README.md.
Write a bash one-liner that lists the .js files in this folder.
Add a function add(a, b) to math.js.
Read config.json and tell me the port.
Write fizzbuzz in Python up to 30.
Append the line 'done' to todo.txt.
Make a folder called src and move app.js into it.
What does the function parse in parser.js do?
Write a small JavaScript script that counts the words in story.txt.
Replace all tabs with two spaces in main.py.
Make the model you trained obsessed with the Golden Gate Bridge.
Train yourself a small model that can use your tools.
Fine-tune the 1B on these examples.
Search the web for the latest llama.cpp release notes.
What's the weather in San Francisco right now?
Download the TinyStories dataset from Hugging Face.
Run this benchmark on an H100 and tell me the throughput.
Summarize today's news about AI.
Write a detailed 3,000-word essay on the history of Rome.
Generate an image of a cat riding a bicycle.
Translate this legal contract into Japanese with careful legal terminology.
Install PyTorch with CUDA and train a classifier on CIFAR-10.
Check whether example.com is up right now.
Look up the price of Bitcoin today.
Prove this math conjecture step by step and double-check every step.

borderline.message: Write a Python script that fetches the weather from an API (just write it, don't run it).
pip install requests and use it to call the GitHub API.
git push my changes to GitHub.
Write unit tests for the add function in math.js and run them.
Refactor this 2,000-line file into well-designed modules with full test coverage.
Write a haiku about the Moon into moon.txt.
Explain in depth how transformer attention works, with the math.
Why does my test in test.js fail? Read it and fix it.
